_help: max_eur = the most this card is worth to you second-hand (EUR). Effective ceiling = min(budget_eur, max_eur). Values are Nov-2026 estimates from eBay sold-price trackers minus ~10% (Cyprus has no buyer protection) - tune them with: python gpu_alert.py --list. Keep the real value even when it is above budget_eur (the ceiling stays at the budget): scam_ratio is measured against max_eur, so a '4090' for 266 is recognised as a fake. The values above 600 are about 10% under the cheapest real used offers on eBay delivered to Cyprus on 2026-11-12.

ebay._help: Official eBay Browse API. Runs only after you store your developer keys with: python gpu_alert.py --setup-ebay. Searches Buy It Now listings that ship to deliver_to, newest first, at most budget_eur. price = item + shipping (+ non_eu_import_vat_pct for sellers outside the EU). ceiling_factor multiplies gpus[].max_eur for eBay only: eBay has buyer protection, so 1.1 means paying up to the full used value. Use euro marketplaces only (EBAY_DE, EBAY_IT, EBAY_FR, EBAY_ES, EBAY_NL, EBAY_AT...).
ebay._help_skip: skip_suspiciously_cheap: on eBay a card under scam_ratio x its used value (gpus[].max_eur, not capped by the budget) is in practice a cooler, box, photo or fake, so it is dropped instead of alerted. Set false to get those alerts with a warning instead.

shops._help: Cypriot computer shops (new cards, a few refurbished). Read every every_minutes in the background, at each shop's robots.txt crawl-delay, with an honest bot user agent. Only cards you can order now are compared with the ceilings. ceiling_factor multiplies gpus[].max_eur for shops only: 1.0 keeps your rule of never paying more than the used value; a new card with warranty may be worth e.g. 1.15. Set a shop to false to stop reading it. needy.shop is not supported (its terms forbid scraping).

business._help: Second buyer: a friend's VAT-registered family business that reclaims the VAT on shop invoices. For shop listings only (a VAT invoice is needed), any card from gpus[] whose shop price falls min_drop_pct or more below the first price the bot saw, with the price without VAT at or under budget_eur, is alerted as [BUSINESS PRICE DROP]. Each cut alerts once; again only after a further 3% drop. Set enabled to false to stop.
business.name: the business

pcs._help: Complete desktop PCs. The bot reads the graphics card, processor and RAM an advert names, prices each at what it costs USED when bought on its own (the tables below), adds rest_eur for the board, PSU, case and SSD, and alerts when the PC costs at most max_price_ratio x that sum (1.05 = up to 5% more than the parts bought one by one; 1.0 = no dearer than the parts; 0.85 = only PCs at least 15% cheaper). The alert says how the price compares, and GREAT DEAL marks PCs at least 16% cheaper than their parts. A PC seen earlier that qualifies only after you loosen these settings alerts once. A part the advert does not name counts as 0, so a vague advert never looks cheap. budget_eur: null = no price cap. A PC only counts with a graphics card from your 12GB+ list (gpus[]), or with a processor worth min_cpu_eur or more plus at least min_ram_gb of RAM (a strong base to add your own card to); smaller cards still add their value to the sum. Sources: the desktop sections of bazaraki and vendora every every_minutes, and (shops: true) the complete PCs of the four shops every shops_every_minutes. For bazaraki adverts whose title leaves parts open the seller's description is read once (at most detail_fetches_per_scan adverts per scan, only above details_min_price).
pcs._help_prices: All part prices: used Buy It Now offers on eBay Germany, lower quartile, measured 2026-11-12 (new-card shop prices where a used one costs more). They are market prices, not the stricter gpus[].max_eur ceilings. Refresh them every few weeks. ram_eur_per_gb: desktop RAM per GB. rest_eur by platform age: old = Intel up to 7th gen, mid = Intel 8th-11th gen and Ryzen 1000-5000 (AM4), new = Intel 12th-14th gen, top = Ryzen 7000+ (AM5) and Core Ultra 200. cpu_eur keys: i5-12 = Core i5 12th gen, r7-5 = Ryzen 7 5000 series, x3d-7 = Ryzen 7000 X3D, u7-2 = Core Ultra 7 200. Intel 12th-14th gen RAM counts as DDR4 unless the advert says DDR5.
pcs._help_oem: Brand-name PCs (title matches oem_title_pattern) get at most rest_eur.oem for the rest: their boards, PSUs and cases are proprietary, often cannot take or power a big graphics card, and are worth little.
pcs._help_other_gpus: Cards below your 12GB rule. They never alert on their own; they only add their value to a PC.

parts._help: Single parts for a platform upgrade: processors, motherboards, desktop RAM and SSDs, plus processor + board (+ RAM) bundles. Every part on the lists below has a reference price = the cheapest it costs NEW in Cyprus. You get an alert when a local advert (bazaraki, vendora) costs at most max_price_ratio x that price (0.75 = at least a quarter cheaper than new), an eBay offer delivered to Cyprus at most ebay_price_ratio x, or a shop's own price at most shops_price_ratio x. GREAT DEAL marks anything at or under 80% of that ceiling. shop_cut_pct: a shop that cuts a watched part by this many percent since the bot first saw it alerts as [SHOP PRICE CUT] even when it stays above the ceiling (0 = off). A processor that is not in cpu_eur and a chipset that is not in board_eur never alert. RAM: desktop DDR4 / DDR5 with ram_min_gb or more in total, priced per GB; laptop (SO-DIMM) and server (ECC) RAM is skipped, and so is DDR4 slower than ram_min_mhz.ddr4. SSD: internal drives of ssd_min_gb or more, priced by capacity class (the keys of ssd_eur are GB). A bundle is compared with the sum of its parts and only counts when its processor is on the list. A local advert under scam_ratio x the new price is tagged SUSPICIOUSLY CHEAP; a shop or eBay item under junk_ratio x the new price is skipped (an accessory for the part, an empty box or a fake), and so is an eBay listing with several variants (its price is that of the cheapest variant).
parts._help_sources: bazaraki's processor, motherboard, RAM and SSD sections (bazaraki_pages each) plus vendora (its component feed and vendora_searches) every every_minutes. eBay through the official API every ebay_every_minutes, sellers in the EU only unless ebay_eu_sellers_only is false. The four shops: one kind of part per run every shops_every_minutes (processors, boards, RAM, SSDs in turn), so each kind is refreshed about every 4 hours. The first read of each source only writes what it finds to alerts.log (marked FIRST READ) instead of sending it to you.
parts._help_generation: The build should last many years, so the current generation is preferred: the sockets, RAM type and SSD interface in current_generation alert at the normal ratios. Everything else on the lists (AM4 and LGA1700 processors and boards, DDR4, SATA SSDs) is an older generation: its ceiling is multiplied by older_generation_ratio (0.8 = an older part must be at least 40% under its new price in a local advert), so it only shows up when it is a very good deal, and shop price cuts are not reported for it. Set older_generation_ratio to 1.0 to treat all generations alike.
parts._help_prices: All prices: the cheapest NEW price in stock in Cyprus on 2026-11-16 (Armenius, Bionic, Custom PC, ComputerG and the dealers on bazaraki). Parts no longer sold new (Ryzen 5700X3D, 5900X, 7600X3D, 7950X; B450, X470, X570, X670, B660, H670, Z690 boards) carry an estimate, and an older model is never priced above a newer, faster one. Used prices on eBay were no use as a reference: delivered to Cyprus they were higher than new parts bought here. Prices move fast in this RAM and SSD shortage, so refresh the tables every few weeks. cpu_eur keys are model numbers: Ryzen 4 digits, Intel Core 5 digits, Core Ultra 3 digits; an Intel F model without its own entry is priced like the model with graphics. board_eur: the cheapest board with that chipset. ram_eur_per_gb: desktop kits per GB. ssd_eur: per capacity class in GB.
